questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: What ultimately made me apply to Boston University was the great travel reports from previous students. Compared to other universities I looked at people were really happy with it. I also wanted to experience the student environment in Boston.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had an amazing time with great courses and got to see some cool stuff.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once I arrived there was a lot of information. It can be hard to sort through but you will get everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I corresponded with coordinator through email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was delayed so missed the orientation. But I was happy with the guidance I got through email.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing is very hit and miss. I stayed in the Hyatt hotel across the river which I really enjoyed. But some of the housing is apperently not that nice and quite expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The meal plan is expensive but in my opinion you also get a lot of value. I came to really enjoy it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is expensive but a lot of the social life with other exchange students were on campus. But you can easily live off campus as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought the options were very expensive but that is how it is in the US. I ended up living in a hotel with cleaning of the room etc. so it was really great for me. I don't know if I would have been as happy living in the student housing with the undergraduates.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You do get help but there is so much information and many different websites so it felt very overwhelming for me. Just take your time with it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration itself is not that hard although you need to get an academic statement from a professor. The course registration is a bit more difficult because you have to acquire the course description from the professors. But don't worry too much as you can add and drop classes for several weeks after the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an international coordinator who was helpful to me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful. Don't worry too much about it. You can also just try and go to a class which is full and speak with the professor. Sometimes they will let you in if you are really interested.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about auditing a language course. You can follow courses without getting grades and it is a free way to get language classes. Take it one step at the time and don't stress. Everything will sort itself out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some great professors and courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two full MA courses and one with a mixture of BA and MA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is way more interaction with the professor and presentations etc depending on the class. For me personally it was a lot better for my learning. You get to know the professors. This is especially the case with higher level courses I think.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Diplomacy and Negotiation with Professor Storella, Topics in international relations - Weapons and War in Europe with Samuel Seitz, Global Money with Perry Mehrling

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend them all. You get to interact a lot with the teacher on specific topics. Diplomacy and Negotiation is fun as there are a lot of exercises. Global Money is probably the most eye opening and I would strongly recommend Perry Mehrling's classes. Weapons and War in Europe is something I am interested in but it is also a demanding class in terms of readings and a large final assignment.

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not realize just how much money everything really cost in the US.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Things were generally more expensive then I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of good opportunities for activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get coaching in different sports at the student fitness center.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join sports clubs and maybe a student association. They have consulting groups, investement groups, arts groups - everything you might like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to around boston and to cape cod. Go to a baseball game with the red sox for 9 dollars with student discount.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Boston is quite european.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Local students were really nice and I made a lot of american friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing major.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are so outgoing and it is easy to get to know new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about your courses, apply for grants before you go, meet some american students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: For political science students there is a gruadate lounge in the basement of the Pardee School of Global Studies. I met a lot of cool people there and they host different academic, social and work related functions. Here I ment american students as well as internationals on who were studying for a degree at BU. Was a great way to get a network outside of the exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of being taught in a more engaging way than have been my experience at UCPH

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting all the paperwork in order. The visa, grant applications and everything else is a lot of work.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
